text:
Broker: So, you have eleven employees, and you're thinking of offering group health coverage for the first time.
Owner: Right. I've been told it can be expensive. I'd like to keep it under four hundred a month per person if possible.
Broker: With eleven employees you'd qualify as a small group. Employer contribution of at least fifty percent is typical. A silver-level plan runs around five hundred and ten per month for an individual. If you pay sixty percent, that's about two hundred and four per employee from you.
Owner: And employees would pay the rest?
Broker: Yes, through payroll deduction. You can also offer a plan with a higher deductible, which brings the premium down to four hundred and ten.
Owner: What about dependents?
Broker: Optional. Usually the employer covers less there, maybe thirty percent. Also, you need seventy percent participation, so at least eight of eleven need to sign up.
Owner: Okay. Let me talk to the team. Can you send me a comparison sheet?
Broker: Of course. I'll put together three options by Thursday.

metadata.note: Insurance broker consultation for small business group coverage
